Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x-3z,\,y,\,z+3x⟩$ and the boundary $S$ of a spherical solid of radius $2$ centered at the origin. Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S.$
question.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

For a sphere or radius $r$ centered at $O,$ the unit normal to the sphere is given by

$$
n=\frac{⟨x,y,z⟩}{r}.
$$

In our case, we have $r=2.$ Therefore,

$$
n=\frac{1}{2}⟨x,y,z⟩.
$$

Using the fact that ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=4$ on $S,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨x-3z,\,y,\,z+3x⟩\cdot \frac{1}{2}⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨x-3z,\,y,\,z+3x⟩\cdot ⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(x(x-3z)+{y}^{2}+z(z+3z)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({x}^{2}-3xz+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}+3xz) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across $S$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}2\,\text{d}S \\  & =2{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S \\  & =2\cdot \text{Area}(S) \\  & =2\cdot 4\pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =32\pi \end{aligned}
$$
